label: Late original-phase token-evidence accumulator (n/h/l/o/f/v/r/w input after v/c/y/a/q/t history)
explanation: Fires only during the original (input) phase, never at t=0/1, on the delimiter, or anywhere in the copy phase. Within the original phase, the firing rate climbs with position (orig_idx 2: 3%, orig_idx 7-8: about 37%) and is highest on the last few tokens before <DEL>. Whether it fires looks additive: the current input token (n is strongest at 4.7x lift, then h, l, o, f, v, r, w), plus how many of v/c/y/a/q/t appeared earlier in the sequence, plus lateness. First occurrences of a token fire more than repeats (1.6x vs 0.3x lift). The top activations are almost all on n, typically late and after earlier v/c/y/t. The additive-score predicate catches most of the activation mass but only about half of its predictions are active, because the true weighting is graded across many tokens. No single clean condition captures it.
